note: Things of a standard size, for the measure tool: something in a picture whose real size is known gives the picture its scale. Sizes are in millimetres and are the ones the named standard or issuer publishes. A size that differs from country to country is not listed as if it did not. Edit freely; a size given on the command line needs no entry here.

card.is: a bank or ID card, long side
card.source: ISO/IEC 7810, card size ID-1: 85.60 x 53.98 mm

card-short.is: a bank or ID card, short side
card-short.source: ISO/IEC 7810, card size ID-1: 85.60 x 53.98 mm

plate-eu.is: a one-line car number plate 520 mm wide, as in Germany and Poland
plate-eu.source: Germany: 520 x 110 mm at most (FZV, Anlage 4); Poland: 520 x 114 mm (Dz.U. 2024 poz. 1709). Many European countries use this width and some do not: check the country, and use the width only

plate-us.is: a North American number plate, width
plate-us.source: AAMVA License Plate Standard: 12 x 6 inches

pallet.source: EPAL Euro pallet: 800 x 1,200 x 144 mm

pallet-short.source: EPAL Euro pallet: 800 x 1,200 x 144 mm

pallet-height.source: EPAL Euro pallet: 800 x 1,200 x 144 mm

container-height.is: a freight container of standard height (a high cube is 2896 mm)
container-height.source: ISO 668: 2,591 mm; a high cube is 2,896 mm

rail-gauge.is: standard-gauge railway track, between the rails
rail-gauge.source: European standard nominal track gauge, 1,435 mm (Regulation (EU) No 1299/2014); not every railway uses it

aa.is: an AA battery, length (the most the standard allows)
aa.source: IEC size R6, as makers' datasheets give it: at most 14.5 x 50.5 mm

golf-ball.is: a golf ball, diameter (the least the rules allow)
golf-ball.source: R&A Equipment Rules: not less than 42.67 mm
